definitions.gloss: classical allusion; literary reference; historical precedent
definitions.explanation: A reference to a classic text, historical event, or well-known story from the literary tradition, especially Chinese classics.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{典故|てんこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This expression has a classical allusion behind it.

examples.japanese: {典故|てんこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{調|しら}べて→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{理解|りかい}した→理解する：06059_rikaisuru⟧。
examples.english: I looked up the classical reference and understood the meaning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢詩|かんし}→漢詩：13438_kanshi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{中国|ちゅうごく}→中国：28300_chuugoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{典故|てんこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{数多|かずおお}く→数多く：12948_kazuooku⟧⟦{含|ふく}まれている→含む：01982_fukumu⟧。
examples.english: Chinese poetry contains many allusions derived from classical Chinese texts.

notes:
Composed of {典|てん} (classic; canon) + {故|こ} (reason; origin; old). Refers to the practice of embedding references to classical literature, history, or philosophy in writing. Particularly common in discussions of ⟦{漢詩|かんし}→漢詩：13438_kanshi⟧ (Chinese poetry), ⟦{和歌|わか}→和歌：05230_waka⟧ (classical Japanese poetry), and literary criticism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {典故|てんこ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{基|もと}づく→基づく：02315_motozuku⟧: to be based on a classical allusion
- {典故|てんこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}く→引く：01978_hiku⟧: to cite a classical reference
- {典故|てんこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{踏|ふ}まえる→踏まえる：07701_fumaeru⟧: to draw on a classical allusion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{故事|こじ}→故事：12944_koji⟧: historical anecdote; precedent — refers to the stories and events themselves, while {典故|てんこ} emphasizes the act of alluding to them in writing
- ⟦{出典|しゅってん}→出典：06424_shutten⟧: source; citation — refers to the specific text being quoted, while {典故|てんこ} refers to the allusive technique
- ⟦{引用|いんよう}→引用：01850_inyou⟧: quotation; citation — a direct quote from a source, while {典故|てんこ} is an indirect allusion
